material_systems.name: DTM Primer for Steel Exterior Doors

products: Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial DTM Acrylic Primer
PPG Pitt-Tech Plus DTM Industrial Primer
primer.notes: Rust-inhibitive DTM primer for bare carbon steel doors. For factory-primed steel in good condition, this primer is used only when factory primer is compromised or bare metal is exposed. Zinc-rich epoxy for severely corroded bare steel; universal acrylic DTM for factory-primed steel needing re-prime. Galvanized steel doors: vinyl wash or acrylic etching primer variant. CRITICAL: bare ferrous metal MUST be primed same day as surface prep — rust begins within hours.

material_systems.notes: Primary primer for steel doors with compromised or absent factory primer. Factory-primed steel in good condition (SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY) may skip field prime and go direct to finish if adhesion test passes. Coverage rate is for smooth steel — consistent, non-porous surface.

material_systems.name: 100% Acrylic Latex Primer for Fiberglass and Wood Doors

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec EXT Primer
PPG Sun Proof Exterior Latex Primer
primer.notes: Standard 100% acrylic exterior primer for fiberglass and wood doors. MANDATORY for fiberglass — oil-based/alkyd primers PROHIBITED due to outgassing blister risk. Acrylic primer is permeable, allowing trapped manufacturing gases to escape. For wood: general primer for non-tannin species; spot-prime knots separately with alkyd on tannin-rich species before this full coat. Coverage assumes smooth factory-finish or sanded door surface.

material_systems.notes: Primary primer for fiberglass and bare wood doors. Fiberglass factory primer is typically compatible with 100% acrylic topcoat — factory-primed fiberglass in good condition may skip field prime. Wood doors always get full field prime on all six sides.

material_systems.name: Alkyd/Shellac Spot Primer for Tannin Knots on Wood Doors

primer.type: Stain-blocking alkyd or shellac-based spot primer
products: KILZ Original Multi-Surface Stain Blocking Primer
primer.notes: Spot-applied to visible knots on tannin-rich species (mahogany, cedar, redwood, Douglas fir) BEFORE full acrylic primer coat. Not a full-surface system — applied per knot/stain location by brush. Alkyd has superior tannin stain blocking vs acrylic. Shellac-based (BIN) for extreme cases. Per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md section 2: spot prime knots with alkyd before acrylic primer over remaining surface.

material_systems.notes: Conditional on wood species — required for tannin-rich species (mahogany, cedar, redwood, fir). Applied by brush to individual knots before full acrylic primer coat. Quantity is not SF-based — it is per-knot consumption.

material_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Door Paint

products: PPG Sun Proof Exterior Acrylic Latex
finish.notes: Mid-grade 100% acrylic exterior enamel for QT3 door painting. Good durability, color retention, mildew resistance. Sheen is project-level selection (satin, semi-gloss, or gloss) — no locked-in default. Two coats standard on primed surfaces. Fiberglass doors: 100% acrylic ONLY — no alkyd or oil-modified formulations.

material_systems.notes: Standard exterior door finish for QT3. Coverage is for smooth primed door surface — consistent and predictable. NOT a fine-finish interior system — standard exterior grade. Door surface is smooth and non-porous after priming, yielding higher coverage than rough siding.

material_systems.name: Premium Exterior Door Paint

finish.notes: Premium acrylic enamel with enhanced UV resistance, color retention, and hardness. QT4: light sand between coats (220-grit), raking light inspection before second coat. QT5: spray in controlled environment (door removed to shop/garage), hand-sand between all coats, DFT verification with gauge. Benjamin Moore Aura Grand Entrance is specifically formulated for exterior entry doors. Sheen is project-level selection — no locked-in default.

material_systems.notes: Premium/superior exterior door finish for QT4 and QT5. Higher solids content yields slightly lower coverage per gallon. QT5 may specify architect-matched formulation for showcase entries.

material_systems.name: IR-Reflective Exterior Door Paint for Dark Colors

finish.type: IR-Reflective Acrylic with Complex Inorganic Color Pigments (CICPs)
products: Benjamin Moore IR-reflective exterior colors (select palette)
finish.notes: MANDATORY for dark colors (LRV < 30). CICPs absorb visible light for dark visual appearance while reflecting near-infrared radiation, dropping surface temperature 20-30 deg F. Without IR-reflective technology: wood joint failure and warping, steel thermal expansion and joint separation, fiberglass outgassing acceleration. HARD STOP — do not apply standard dark paint (LRV < 30) to any exterior door substrate. Color palette is more limited than standard paint lines.

material_systems.notes: Conditional system — replaces standard or premium finish when color LRV < 30. Applies across all quality tiers and all substrates. Slightly lower coverage than standard acrylic due to specialty CICP pigment formulation. This is not optional — it is a substrate protection requirement, not a cosmetic upgrade.

ea_conversion.notes: Standard entry door: ~20 SF per face x 2 faces + ~4 LF edges x 1.75 in width + frame/jamb. Single slab ~30-35 SF total. Panel door ~35-45 SF total. Grand entry ~45-55 SF total (includes sidelite/transom frames).

SS_EXT_BARE_METAL.notes: Smooth steel surface — non-porous, consistent primer absorption. Coverage based on 40 SF per door assembly at 375 SF/gal.

coverage_profiles.waste_notes: 10% waste factor for door painting — contained environment, minimal overspray on discrete item.
assumptions: Coverage based on smooth steel surface — non-porous, predictable.
Spray application: multiply by 1.20-1.25 for transfer efficiency loss on small-area item (less overshoot than siding).
Dent repair areas may require additional primer locally.

ea_conversion.notes: Same door assembly SF as DTM profile. Wood doors may absorb slightly more at end grain (top/bottom edges).

SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD.notes: Bare wood absorbs more primer than steel — especially at end grain (top/bottom edges for six-side seal). Coverage lower than steel.

coverage_profiles.waste_notes: 10% waste factor. Six-side sealing on wood doors may increase effective material use by 5-10% for edge coverage.
assumptions: Coverage rates are for smooth surfaces — textured fiberglass doors may reduce coverage by 10-15%.
Wood end grain (top and bottom edges) absorbs primer heavily — may need two primer passes on edges.
Fiberglass factory primer in good condition: skip field prime entirely.

ea_conversion.notes: Same assembly SF as primer profiles. Finish coverage is on primed (sealed) surface — more consistent than primer coverage.

SYS_EXT_DOOR_FINISH_STANDARD.notes: Standard acrylic on primed door. Consistent, predictable coverage on sealed surface.

SYS_EXT_DOOR_FINISH_PREMIUM.notes: Premium acrylic-urethane has higher solids — slightly lower coverage per gallon. Better film build per coat.

SYS_EXT_DOOR_FINISH_IR_REFLECTIVE.notes: IR-reflective formulation with CICP pigments — reduced coverage compared to standard acrylic. Specialty pigment formulation.

coverage_profiles.waste_notes: 10% waste factor for door finish coats. Two coats standard at all quality tiers.
assumptions: Coverage is per coat — multiply by 2 for total material per door.
Spray application: multiply material by 1.20-1.25 for transfer efficiency.
Grand entry assemblies at upper end of SF range — sidelite/transom frames add ~10-15 SF.
Gloss sheen may require slightly more material for proper film build than satin.

consumables.name: Airless Spray Tip 310 (steel/fiberglass door faces)
consumables.notes: 310 tip (0.010 inch orifice, 6-inch fan) for metal and fiberglass door faces. Tight fan pattern for precision on discrete item. Also suitable for 412 tip (0.012 inch, 8-inch fan) on larger door faces. Per Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine.md: metal doors use 0.010-0.014 inch orifice. Only applicable when application_method = spray.

consumables.name: Airless Spray Tip 411 (wood door faces)
consumables.notes: 411 tip (0.011 inch orifice, 8-inch fan) for wood door faces. Slightly wider fan than 310 for wood grain coverage. Also suitable for panel door faces. Only applicable when application_method = spray.

consumables.name: 60-Mesh Spray Filter (black) for Latex
consumables.notes: Standard 60-mesh (black) filter for latex exterior coatings through airless equipment. Change when flow rate drops. Only applicable when application_method = spray.

consumables.name: Angled Sash Brush 2.5 inch
consumables.notes: Primary brush for door panel recesses, edges, and detail work. 2.5-inch angular sash for panel doors, glass lite mullion detail, and all 4 edges. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.md: 1 brush per material type. ~5,000 LF lifespan with care. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Flat Brush 2 inch
consumables.notes: Secondary brush for narrow edge painting (top edge, bottom edge, hinge edge, latch edge). 2-inch flat for precision on door edge width. Also used for six-side seal on wood door bottom edge.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 80 Grit
consumables.usage_rate: 1 SHEET per 2 doors (steel dent repair only)
consumables.notes: For steel door dent repair — rough sand before body filler application. Only for steel substrate with dent damage. Not used on fiberglass or wood.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 Grit
consumables.notes: Intercoat sanding between finish coats. QT3: visual inspect only — no intercoat sand. QT4: light scuff sand between finish coats (220-grit). QT5: hand-sand with raking light inspection. Also used for scuff-sanding factory-primed steel doors before topcoat. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320 Grit
consumables.notes: Fine sanding for QT5 intercoat work. Feathering scratch/rust repairs on steel to imperceptible transition (300-320 grit per Exterior_Doors_Doctrine.md section 2). Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Tack Cloth
consumables.notes: Dust removal after sanding before prime or finish coat. Required after all sanding operations. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Xylene or Acetone for Steel Door Solvent Clean
consumables.notes: Solvent cleaning for steel door surfaces — removes manufacturing oils, release agents, and contaminants. Per Exterior_Doors_Doctrine.md section 2: xylene or acetone + TSP detergent wash. Steel substrate only — NOT for fiberglass (damages resin).

consumables.name: TSP or TSP-Substitute Detergent
consumables.notes: TSP detergent wash for steel doors (after solvent clean) and general cleaning on all substrates. Mild dish soap alternative for fiberglass doors. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Two-Component Auto Body Filler (steel door dent repair)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA (quart size) per 4-6 doors with dent repair
consumables.notes: For dent repair on steel doors. Sand 80-grit, fill, finish-sand 240/300-grit. Only for steel substrate with dent damage. Per Exterior_Doors_Doctrine.md section 2. Conditional — most NC steel doors arrive undamaged.

consumables.name: Exterior Wood Filler
consumables.notes: For filling small defects, nail holes, and minor damage on wood doors. Exterior-rated filler that remains flexible. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Glass Masking Film (HDPE static-cling or masking paper)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA kit per door with glass lites
consumables.notes: HDPE static-cling film for glass lites in door slab and sidelites/transom. Covers glass area to protect from spray overspray and brush drips. QT5 alternative: liquid mask for razor-sharp paint lines at glass edge. Per-door, not per-lite — one kit covers all glass in a door assembly. Grand entry with sidelites and transom uses larger quantity.

consumables.name: Painter's Tape (exterior grade)
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum. Used for glass masking edge seal, threshold protection tape, weatherstrip gap protection, and general edge masking. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.md: all tape rolls yield 180 LF (60 yards). Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Masking Film / Plastic Sheeting
consumables.notes: For threshold protection, entry walkway overspray containment, and adjacent surface protection during spray application. 4 mil minimum for walkway protection. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Canvas Drop Cloths
consumables.notes: Heavy canvas drop cloths for entry walkway/porch/stoop protection below door work area. Non-slip surface for crew traffic. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Hardware Storage Bags with Labels
consumables.notes: Labeled ziplock bags for storing removed door hardware — lockset, deadbolt, strike plates, hinges, address numbers, knocker, mail slot, doorbell. One bag per door minimum. Grand entry with additional hardware may need 2+ bags. Label with door location and hardware contents. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Weatherstrip Protection Tape
consumables.notes: Low-tack tape pushed deep into weatherstrip gap with putty knife when friction-fit stripping cannot be removed. Protects weatherstripping from paint contamination. Per Exterior_Doors_Doctrine.md section 6: never paint weatherstripping. 180 LF per roll at ~30 LF per door perimeter.

ext_door_glass_mask.description: Glass lites in door slab and sidelites/transom requiring masking during door painting
ext_door_glass_mask.notes: Masking tape for edge seal at glass-to-frame junction + masking film over glass area. Grand entry with sidelites and transom requires significantly more masking material and time than standard half-lite door. This spec owns glass masking when painting the DOOR itself — distinct from trim spec which masks glass adjacent to CASING.

ext_door_hardware.description: Door hardware removal, storage, and reinstallation
ext_door_hardware.notes: Hardware is REMOVED per doctrine — not masked. Areas beneath hardware must be sealed to prevent moisture infiltration. Standard door = 1 hardware group (lockset + deadbolt + strike plates + hinges). Grand entry may have additional items (knocker, mail slot, doorbell, address numbers).

ext_door_weatherstrip.description: Weatherstrip protection — pull out friction-fit or deep-tape non-removable
ext_door_weatherstrip.notes: Every exterior door has weatherstripping. Friction-fit stripping: gently pull out, re-insert after finish is dry. Non-removable stripping: deep-tape into gap with putty knife. Tape consumed only when stripping cannot be removed. 1:1 with door count.

ext_door_threshold.description: Door threshold/sill protection from drips and overspray
ext_door_threshold.notes: Tape and plastic over threshold to catch drips during door edge and face painting. Especially important during bottom edge painting (both brush and spray). 1:1 with door count.

ext_hardscape_walk.notes: Canvas drop cloths for non-slip crew traffic on entry walkway. Plastic sheeting for spray overspray containment. Protection scope is limited to immediate entry area — not full-elevation landscape protection (siding spec scope).

compatibility_rules.description: DTM primer required for bare steel doors
compatibility_rules.notes: Standard acrylic primer on bare steel causes flash rust. DTM primer has rust-inhibitive pigments. CRITICAL: must prime same day as bare metal exposure.

compatibility_rules.description: 100% acrylic ONLY on fiberglass doors — oil-based/alkyd prohibited
compatibility_rules.notes: Oil-based coatings strictly not recommended on fiberglass per Exterior_Doors_Doctrine.md section 3. Non-breathable oil coatings trap manufacturing gases under sun heat, causing outgassing blisters — the number 1 failure mode on fiberglass doors. Only 100% acrylic systems permitted.

compatibility_rules.description: Tannin knot spot-prime required for tannin-rich wood species
compatibility_rules.notes: Alkyd/shellac spot primer on visible knots before full acrylic primer coat. Prevents tannin bleed staining through finish. Not required for non-tannin species (pine, poplar, maple).

compatibility_rules.description: IR-reflective finish MANDATORY for dark colors (LRV < 30)
compatibility_rules.notes: HARD STOP for all substrates when color LRV < 30. Without IR-reflective technology: wood joint failure, steel thermal expansion/warping, fiberglass outgassing acceleration. Per Exterior_Doors_Doctrine.md section 3 and Exterior_Color_Sheen_Configuration_Doctrine.md sections 1-2.

compatibility_rules.description: Factory-primed steel/fiberglass may skip field prime
compatibility_rules.notes: Factory-primed steel and fiberglass doors in good condition with passing adhesion test may skip field prime and go direct to finish coats. This differs from fiber cement siding where field prime over factory prime is ALWAYS required. Light degloss/scuff of factory primer before topcoat is still required.

compatibility_rules.description: Field-primed surfaces skip prime module entirely
compatibility_rules.notes: Direct topcoat application on field-primed surfaces. Skip prime module entirely.

compatibility_rules.description: Six-side sealing mandatory for wood doors
compatibility_rules.notes: All six sides of wood door must be finished within 2-4 weeks. Unsealed end-grain (top/bottom edges) causes massive moisture wicking and swelling. Bottom edge is particularly critical — prop open during cure. Failure to seal = warranty voidance. Per Exterior_Doors_Doctrine.md sections 5 and 7.

compatibility_rules.description: No sanding of textured fiberglass doors
compatibility_rules.notes: Do NOT sand textured (stain-grade) fiberglass doors — destroys the wood-grain profile. Paint-grade (smooth) fiberglass can be lightly scuffed for adhesion. Per Exterior_Doors_Doctrine.md section 2.

compatibility_rules.description: Steel door gloss caution per ANSI A250.8
compatibility_rules.notes: Steel doors per ANSI A250.8 (SDI 100): maximum paint gloss = 20% reflectance at 60-degree gloss meter. High gloss emphasizes factory welding marks and surface imperfections. Semi-gloss or satin recommended for steel doors. Not a prohibition — customer must be informed of show-through risk.

NEVER use hydrocarbon-based solvents (xylene, acetone, mineral spirits) on fiberglass — damages resin matrix. Clean fiberglass with mild dish soap or denatured alcohol only. Per Exterior_Doors_Doctrine.md section 2.

risk_notes.topic: Fiberglass outgassing blisters from oil-based coatings
risk_notes.risk: Oil-based paints on fiberglass doors trap manufacturing vapors released over years. Non-breathable oil coatings trap gas under sun heat, creating blisters that rupture the paint film.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use ONLY 100% acrylic latex enamel on fiberglass doors. No oil-based, alkyd, or oil-modified products. Coating must be permeable.

risk_notes.topic: Dark color thermal damage without IR-reflective coating
risk_notes.risk: Standard dark paint (LRV < 30) on exterior doors causes excessive heat absorption: wood warping and joint failure, steel thermal expansion and joint separation, fiberglass accelerated outgassing.
risk_notes.mitigation: MANDATORY IR-reflective (CICPs) coating for ALL exterior doors with color LRV < 30. HARD STOP — no exceptions.

risk_notes.topic: Bare steel flash rust from delayed priming
risk_notes.risk: Bare ferrous metal begins rusting within hours of surface preparation in humid conditions. Any delay between prep and prime voids the surface prep and requires re-prep.
risk_notes.mitigation: Prime bare steel SAME DAY as surface preparation. Schedule prep and prime as continuous task — do not break across days.

risk_notes.topic: Wood door moisture wicking from unsealed end grain
risk_notes.risk: Rails (top/bottom edges) act as capillary networks. Unsealed end-grain absorbs moisture, causing massive swelling, joint separation, and paint film rupture. Voids manufacturer warranty.
risk_notes.mitigation: Six-side sealing of all wood doors within 2-4 weeks of installation. Bottom edge is particularly critical. Auto-add six-side sealing task for all wood door specs.

risk_notes.topic: Tannin bleed through finish on wood doors
risk_notes.risk: Mahogany, cedar, redwood, and fir species bleed tannins through standard acrylic primer, causing brown/yellow staining on finish coat.
risk_notes.mitigation: Spot-prime visible knots with alkyd or shellac-based primer (SYS_EXT_DOOR_PRIMER_TANNIN_SPOT) before full acrylic primer coat.

risk_notes.risk: Rust painted over continues electrolytic action beneath film. Moisture travels via capillary action under primer, causing progressive delamination.
risk_notes.mitigation: Remove all active oxidation to bare metal using SSPC-SP3 (power tool cleaning) or SSPC-SP6 (commercial blast cleaning). Prime immediately.

risk_notes.risk: High gloss on steel doors (ANSI A250.8) emphasizes factory welding marks, seam lines, and surface imperfections that are invisible at lower sheens.
risk_notes.mitigation: Recommend semi-gloss or satin for steel doors. If customer insists on gloss, document show-through risk and consider additional prep (body filler for surface leveling).

risk_notes.risk: Paint on weatherstripping destroys elasticity, causes brittleness and seal tearing. Results in air/water infiltration at door perimeter.
risk_notes.mitigation: Remove friction-fit stripping before painting. Deep-tape non-removable stripping. Never paint over weatherstrip material.

material_quantity_notes.ea_based_system: This spec uses EA (each) as the primary UOM. Material quantities are calculated per door assembly, not per SF. Each door assembly includes both faces, all 4 edges, and frame/jamb. Standard entry door = ~40 SF total paintable area.

sf_per_door_by_complexity.single_slab: 30-35 SF (flat flush door, both faces + 4 edges + frame)
sf_per_door_by_complexity.panel: 35-45 SF (raised panel adds recessed surface area)

material_quantity_notes.waste_factor: 10% material waste for door painting — discrete contained item with minimal overspray waste. Lower than siding (15%) or trim (15%) due to controlled application environment.
material_quantity_notes.spray_transfer_efficiency: Airless spray on doors: 75-80% transfer efficiency (better than siding due to close-range application on flat surface). Multiply theoretical coverage by 1.20-1.25.
material_quantity_notes.two_coat_standard: Standard coat system: 1 prime + 2 finish coats on bare substrates. Factory-primed steel/fiberglass in good condition: 2 finish coats only (skip prime). Field-primed: 2 finish coats only.
material_quantity_notes.six_side_seal_wood: Wood doors require primer and finish on ALL six sides. Bottom edge is primary moisture entry point — must be painted with door propped open and allowed to cure before closing.
material_quantity_notes.grand_entry_material_premium: Grand entry assemblies consume ~30-50% more material than single slab due to sidelite/transom frame painting and additional edge work.

assumptions.value: ~40 SF per standard entry door assembly (both faces + 4 edges + frame/jamb)
assumptions.source: Exterior_Doors_Doctrine.md section 4; User brief; industry standard door sizing (3068 = 36x80 inches)
assumptions.note: Doctrine provides hours/EA rates but does not specify SF per door. SF estimate derived from standard door dimensions: 2 faces at ~20 SF each = 40 SF + edges + frame = ~40-45 SF total. Used for material quantity conversion only.

assumptions.value: Factory-primed steel/fiberglass doors may skip field prime (unlike fiber cement siding)
assumptions.note: Exterior_Substrates_Doctrine.md mandates field prime over factory prime for fiber cement. Door doctrine implies factory-primed steel/fiberglass may be adequate — different substrate behavior. Flagged as assumption pending explicit doctrine clarification for door substrates.
No doctrine-specific coverage for IR-reflective door paint. Derived from sibling trim spec solar-reflective coverage and product data. CICP pigment formulation reduces coverage vs standard acrylic.

assumptions.value: 300-400 SF/gal for premium acrylic-urethane door paint
assumptions.note: No doctrine-specific coverage for premium door finish. Derived from sibling trim spec premium finish coverage. Higher solids = slightly lower coverage.

assumptions.source: Industry standard; Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.md section on waste (10-20% wastage allowance)
assumptions.note: Doctrine states 10-20% wastage allowance. Using 10% for doors because discrete contained items have less waste than field siding/trim. Sibling specs use 15% for siding and trim.

uncertainty_flags.description: Resolution indicates factory-primed steel/fiberglass doors may skip field prime. No clear doctrine defines the adhesion test threshold for this decision. Field practice varies.
uncertainty_flags.action: Flag for field calibration. Consider adding adhesion test protocol (ASTM D3359 cross-hatch tape pull) as explicit decision gate.

uncertainty_flags.description: Grand entry door assembly SF estimate (45-55 SF) is extrapolated from standard door dimensions plus estimated sidelite/transom frame area. Actual assemblies vary widely.
uncertainty_flags.action: Validate against field measurements of actual grand entry assemblies. May need per-component SF breakdown.

uncertainty_flags.description: Spray tip selection for fiberglass doors not explicitly addressed in Application Methods Doctrine (steel door tips are specified). Using similar tip range (310/411) based on similar door face geometry.
uncertainty_flags.action: Validate fiberglass spray tip selection against field practice. Textured fiberglass may benefit from slightly larger orifice.
